title: Contrast Ultrasound Targeted Treatment of Gliomas in Mice via Drug-Bearing Nanoparticle Delivery and Microvascular Ablation
protocol: Place a 1% solution of serum albumin in normal saline in a flask with an octafluoropropane gas blanket above the aqueous phase.
Sonicate the albumin solution for 30 seconds using an ultrasound disintegrator equipped with an extended titanium probe.
Determine mean microbubble diameter with a Multisizer Coulter Counter.
Fabricate lipid microbubbles by preparing an aqueous dispersion of polyethyleneglycol-40 stearate and distearoyl phosphatidylcholine.
Sonicate the lipid solution for 30 seconds using an ultrasound disintegrator equipped with an extended titanium probe.
Determine mean lipid microbubble diameter with a Multisizer Coulter Counter.
Prepare a 2% Poly(vinyl alcohol) PVA solution by dissolving 20g of PVA in 1000 ml of deionized water overnight on a stir plate.
Centrifuge the PVA solution at 1000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Filter the centrifuged PVA solution with a 0.22μm sterile filter to remove undissolved PVA.
Dissolve 180 mg of uncapped 85:15 PLAGA in 6 ml methylene chloride.
Vortex the MC/PLAGA solution for 2 minutes.
Dissolve 15 mg of BSA in 1.5 ml PBS.
Add half of the PBS/BSA solution to the MC/PLAGA solution with intermittent vortexing.
Place the solution on ice for 5 minutes.
Sonicate the solution at 45 W for 120 seconds.
Add the remaining PBS/BSA solution to the MC/PLAGA solution with intermittent vortexing.
Place the solution on ice for 5 minutes.
Sonicate the solution at 45 W for 120 seconds.
Add the MC/PLAGA/payload/PBS solution to 24 ml of 2% PVA in two portions with intermediate vortexing.
Place the solution on ice for 5 minutes.
Sonicate the solution at 45 W for 120 seconds.
Stir the NP emulsion for 12 hours on a stir plate in a fume hood to allow evaporation of MC and NP stabilization.
Centrifuge the suspension for 25 minutes at 20,000 rpm at 4°C twice to isolate NPs and remove residual PVA.
Resuspend the pellet in 8 ml of DI water.
Centrifuge the resuspended sample for 10 minutes at 1000 rpm at 4°C to isolate the 100 nm population of NPs.
Isolate the supernatant containing isolated nanoparticles.
Flash freeze the supernatant at -80°C.
Lyophilize the frozen sample for 48 hours.
Store the lyophilized particles in a dessicator at -80°C until time of use.
Combine one vial of VivoTag680 with 50 μL of 1.0 M HEPES, pH 7 and Succinic anhydride (2.5 mg) in DMSO.
Add 50 μL of 1.0 M NaOH to the solution; mix thoroughly.
Allow the solution to react for 2 hours at room temperature protected from light.
Purify particles using Bio-Rad BioGel P100 medium eluting with 0.1 M MES buffer, pH 6.0; collect the green band.
Combine carboxy-modified VivoTag680 obtained in 0.1 M MES buffer, pH 6, with EDC and Sulfo-NHS.
Allow to react for 2 hours at room temperature.
Purify activated particles from excess activating agent by gel filtration using Bio-Rad BioGel P100 medium eluting with 0.1 M MES buffer, pH 6.0; collect the green band.
Conjugate activated particles to amine-containing molecules (e.g., BSA-loaded Nanoparticle).
Allow the solution to react for 2 hours at room temperature.
Purify conjugated nanoparticles from excess EDC by centrifuging at 20,000 rpm for 60 minutes at 4°C; pour off supernatant after centrifugation and resuspend in 0.1 MES buffer.
Combine NP680 obtained in 0.1 M MES buffer, pH 6 with 1 mg of EDC and 2.2 mg of Sulfo-NHS.
Allow the solution to react for 1 hour at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 20,000 rpm for 60 minutes at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend nanoparticles in 0.1 M MES buffer.
Wash albumin MBs three times in degassed PBS to remove excess BSA from solution.
Conjugate activated particles to amine-containing molecules (e.g., Albumin Microbubbles).
Allow NP680 solution to react for 2 hours at room temperature.
Purify NP680 conjugated microbubbles (MNCA) from unbound NP680s by washing three times with degassed PBS.
Inoculate C57BLJ6/Rag1 mice with 3 x 10^6 C6 Glioma tumor cells suspended in 300 μl of PBS subcutaneously in the left hindlimb.
Allow tumor to grow for 12 days to reach a maximum diameter of 8-10 mm.
Anesthetize mice with an intraperitoneal injection of ketamine hydrochloride (60 mg/kg body weight) and xylazine (0.1 mg/kg body weight).
Prepare a maintenance anesthetic consisting of ketamine hydrochloride (20 mg/kg body weight) and xylazine (0.3 mg/kg body weight).
Administer the maintenance anesthetic as needed.
Cannulate the tail vein of each animal for intravenous administration of MB, MB/NP or MNCA solution.
I.V. infuse a lipid MB solution (1x10^8 MBs/g body weight in 0.3 ml of 0.9% saline) at a rate of 15 μl/min using a continuous infusion pump.
Couple the 15L8 probe to the tumor with a water-based ultrasound gel.
Scan the tumor in B-Mode to obtain the best imaging plane.
Acquire a continuous video capturing microbubbles signal intensity.
Capture video 5 seconds prior and 20 seconds following the high-amplitude "burst" pulse at a frame rate of 13Hz.
Repeat measurements in four imaging planes.
Wait ten minutes to infuse albumin MBs and initiate therapeutic low frequency treatment.
Infuse an albumin MB (1 x10^5 MBs/g body weight in 0.3 ml of 0.9% saline).
I.V. infuse MB/NP (1 x10^5 MBs/g and 0.2 ug NPs/g body weight in 0.3 ml of 0.9% saline) or MNCA solution (1 x10^5 MNCAs/g body weight in 0.3 ml of 0.9% saline).
Insonate for sixty minutes with the "1-Burst" pulse sequence during a continuous infusion of NPs, a co-injection of MBs and NPs, or MNCAs.
Amplify the waveform signal by a 55 dB RF.
Use a power amplifier to amplify the waveform signal.
Insert a needle thermocouple probe into the tumor for temperature monitoring.
Record temperature measurements every five minutes during the experiment.
Repeat tumor perfusion measurements ten minutes following therapeutic treatment.
Enter ACQ mode in the CPS program on the Sequoia.
Select the region of interest encompassing the complete tumor volume.
Fit perfusion recovery curves to CPS data.
Evaluate β, a relative measure of red blood cell velocity, pre-treatment and post-treatment.
Export CPS files for off-line analysis.
Convert data into avi files.
Break avi files into frame-by-frame image sequences.
Generate a time averaged image using Compaq Visual Fortan or similar software.
Place mice on a low alfasprot diet twelve days prior to treatment.
Shave the imaging site (flank to liver) to remove all hair.
Remove residual hair with a chemical hair removal agent.
Rinse off all residual chemical hair remover.
Anesthetize mice with an IP combination injection of ketamine hydrochloride and xylazine.
Place mouse on the imaging cartridge.
Acquire reflectance images in white light mode.
Carry out fluorescent tomographic imaging in the VT680 channel.
Employ FMT software to generate 3D reconstructions of imaging data using a normalized Born equation.
Select volumes of interest (VOI) by drawing regions of interest (ROI) in all three imaging planes (X, Y, Z).
Generate mean fluorescent values and total VOI volume for the feet and liver from fluorescently tagged BSA NPs.
Measure tumor volume daily using digital calipers.
Calculate tumor volumes using an ellipsoid approximation: V = 1/6 π abc, where a, b, and c are maximum diameters of the tumor in three orthogonal planes.
Seven days after treatment, euthanize animals.
Cannulate the left ventricle and exsanguinate blood with 2% Heparinized Tris CaCl2 Buffer (0.68mM) for 10 minutes at 100 mmHg.
Perfuse tissue with an additional 10ml of Tris CaCl2 Buffer (0.68mM) for 10 minutes at 100 mmHg.
Perfusion-fix tissue with an infusion of 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS (4°C) for 10 minutes at 100 mmHg.
Allow the sample to fix for an additional 50 minutes after initial perfusion fixation.
Excise tumor specimens and embed them in paraffin.
Cut excised specimens into 5-micron sections.
Perform standard hematoxylin-eosin staining on sections.
Use a terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase mediated deoxyuridine triphosphate nick end labeling (TUNEL) assay to detect apoptotic cells.
Perform the TUNEL assay using the ApoptTag kit from Intergen Co., Norcross, GA, USA.
